description: This topic covers major National Days observed in India and their historical backgrounds. It is crucial for competitive exams where dates, themes, and related eminent personalities are frequently asked.

sections.title: Important Days from January to March
sections.description: Key national days observed in the first quarter of the year and their significance.

key_associations.extra_info: Celebrated to commemorate the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda.
Declared by the Government of India to honor the birth anniversary of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.
Initiated by the Ministry of Women and Child Development to empower girls and raise awareness about their rights.
Celebrated to mark the foundation day of the Election Commission of India in 1950.
Commemorates the discovery of the 'Raman Effect' by Sir C.V. Raman in 1928, for which he won the Nobel Prize.

sections.title: Important Days from April to June
sections.description: Major days during the second quarter related to governance, technology, and statistics.

key_associations.extra_info: Commemorates the day in 1947 when Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel addressed administrative officers as the 'Steel Frame of India'.
Marks the passing of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, which institutionalized Panchayati Raj in India.
Commemorates the successful execution of the Pokhran-II nuclear tests in 1998.
Celebrated on the birth anniversary of the eminent statistician Prof. P.C. Mahalanobis.

sections.title: Important Days from July to September
sections.description: Key dates in the third quarter dedicated to sports, education, healthcare, and national defense.

key_associations.extra_info: Observed to honor the birth and death anniversary of the legendary physician and former West Bengal CM, Dr. Bidhan Chandra Roy.
Commemorates the success of 'Operation Vijay' and honors the martyrs of the 1999 Kargil War.

key_associations.associated_with: National Handloom Day / Javelin Throw Day
key_associations.extra_info: Handloom Day commemorates the Swadeshi Movement (1905). Javelin Throw Day honors Neeraj Chopra's Olympic Gold Medal.
Celebrated on the birth anniversary of the hockey wizard Major Dhyan Chand.
Observed on the birth anniversary of India's second President and esteemed philosopher, Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan.
Marks the day in 1949 when the Constituent Assembly adopted Hindi (in Devanagari script) as the official language of the Union.

sections.title: Important Days from October to December
sections.description: National days in the final quarter marking the legacy of prominent leaders and constitutional milestones.

key_associations.extra_info: Commemorates the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the chief architect of India's political integration.
Observed on the birth anniversary of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, the first Education Minister of independent India.
Marks the adoption of the Indian Constitution (1949) and the birth anniversary of Dr. Verghese Kurien (Father of the White Revolution).
Celebrated on the birth anniversary of the legendary Indian mathematician Srinivasa Ramanujan.
Honors the birth anniversary of farmers' leader and India's 5th Prime Minister, Chaudhary Charan Singh.
Observed on the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

sections.title: Important Facts and Constitutional Aspects
sections.description: Constitutional rules and one-liner facts related to the establishment of these significant days.

polity_articles.provision: The official language of the Union shall be Hindi in Devanagari script.
polity_articles.details: This constitutional provision forms the basis for celebrating Hindi Diwas on September 14.

historical_events.significance: On the 125th birth anniversary of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the Ministry of Social Justice notified November 26 as Constitution Day to promote constitutional values.

important_facts.fact: National Panchayati Raj Day was first declared in 2010 by the then Prime Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh.
In 2021, the Government of India declared August 14 to be observed annually as 'Partition Horrors Remembrance Day'.
Good Governance Day was established in 2014 to foster awareness among citizens regarding accountability in government institutions.
